newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end down, meal falters on cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end down, meal falters on cash.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower Wednesday, with soymeal futures under pressure from weakening cash basis levels and commodity fund selling, pit traders said.
"People are really beginning to notice how meal basis is tanking (going lower)," said one floor trader.
Spot soymeal basis offers have fallen as much as $6.00 per ton since Friday, and some basis values were down as much as $4.00 per ton Wednesday, floor and cash sources said.
In contrast, commodity funds were buying soyoil, which limited losses in that market, traders said.
Commodity funds sold at least 1,100 lots of soymeal and bought at least 800 lots of soyoil, pit traders said.
Some support in soymeal was tied to news that South Korea would tender Monday for 125,000 tonnes of soymeal, traders said.
CBOT soymeal ended down $2.90 to $0.90 per ton, with January down $2.80 at $226.90. Soyoil settled down 0.03 to 0.05 cent per lb, with January down 0.05 at 23.10 cents.
On the day, Chicago Corp sold 800 lots March soymeal, Rand Financial sold 400 March and FIMAT sold 500 lots May.
In soyoil trading, Rand Financial bought 500 lots March, Produce Grain bought 300 March and E.D. and F. Man bought 250 lots March.

Soyoil futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 24,000 contracts, below the 26,084 traded Tuesday. Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, above the 17,124 traded Tuesday, the exchange said.
